messages:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a concrete model-entry pipeline that runs benchmarks, validation, and serving-compat checks before a model is admitted to Dedicated/Hosted. Sketching a staging job that does perf + schema + regressions. Ideas?

devin: +1. Important we include quant-aware perf profiles (int8/qat) and CPU fallback. Also save raw metrics for later analysis.

liam: Split concerns: quality/safety evals vs serving compatibility (kv layout, dtype). Keep them independent so failing a quality eval doesn't block internal compatibility tests.

sophia: Proposed stage sequence: ingest->static-compat->runtime-perf->regressions->package. I'll dump a sample pipeline config below.

sophia: ```yaml
stages:
  - name: metadata
    cmd: python tools/extract_meta.py --model $MODEL
  - name: static_compat
    cmd: scripts/check_compat.sh --require-kv --max-seq 4096
  - name: perf
    cmd: bench-run --profiles cpu,gpu --quant-aware --save-raw ./artifacts/$MODEL
  - name: regressions
    cmd: pytest tests/regressions/test_suite.py::smoke -k $MODEL --junit-xml=./artifacts/regressions.xml
  - name: package
    cmd: tools/package_model --output s3://redwood-models/$MODEL --manifest ./artifacts/manifest.json
```

devin: Perf stage should report p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/s, peak GPU mem, and per-op time breakdown. Also capture sample generation traces for correctness debugging.

bench-bot: auto-report: perf baseline mismatch = 0.87x vs reference; p95 latency +12% :warning: See artifacts: s3://bench-artifacts/1768504321/

liam: For static_compat, tooling needs to check: tensor dtypes, kv cache layout (key/val shapes), expected attention ops. If mismatch -> tag as "serving-incompatible" with details.

ops-bot: packaging note: models intended for Private deploys must be encrypted with customer KMS. Packaging step should include kms_key_id in manifest or fail.

maya: Rollout policy options discussed in RFC — do we want hard block on serving-incompatible? My preference: soft-block for canary/early, hard-block for prod channels. Thoughts?

liam: Soft warn by default, but hard-block for channels that map to customer-facing Dedicated clusters. We should encode channel->policy in the manifest.

sasha: I'll own the regression test harness layout. Plan: small curated prompt sets per domain + automatic sampling. Will store prompt_set_id and results in manifest.

ethan: We must also record tokenizer version/hash with the model manifest. Tokenizer drift causes subtle diffs in evaluation.

maya: Agreed — manifest fields: model_sha256, tokenizer_hash, manifest_version, serving_compat:[tags], perf_baseline_ref, prompt_set_ids. Also kernel_hints for runtime.

devin: Implementation plan: 2-week spike to deliver perf harness + baseline store, then iterate on static compatibility checks. Volunteers?

maya: Volunteers: devin (bench infra), sasha (regressions harness), liam (compat checks), sophia (manifest + packaging). I'll open a JIRA and link the spike. @devin @sasha @liam @sophia

sasha: ack — will sketch repo layout and example prompt sets by EOD tomorrow.

maya: Thanks folks. I'll add the RFC follow-up doc to GH and tag the list. :thumbsup:
